correctness_review.no_fsdp: fsdp_axis=None leaves batch_axes intact, column_storage equals old column_compute, and requested lookup/residual placements coincide.
correctness_review.no_tp: model_axis=None leaves vocabulary replicated; a configured FSDP feature partition and retained independent batch partition are legal.
correctness_review.shared_batch_fsdp: Only fsdp_axis is removed from lookup batch placement, avoiding duplicate use of the same mesh axis in lookup batch/features. Final reshard restores the original batch placement.
correctness_review.independent_fsdp_and_batch: Non-overlapping batch axes are preserved. Lookup output carries both retained batch and feature partitions; final reshard gathers feature placement to existing residual layout.
correctness_review.multiple_batch_axes: Filtering removes only the one configured overlapping FSDP axis and preserves order and all independent axes.
correctness_review.forward_vjp: Uses ordinary differentiable reshard/gather operations; no manual backward or accumulation-dtype substitution. Retained CPU tests check all model gradients and equality of parameter/gradient shardings. Actual TPU scatter order for this extracted candidate has not been independently measured.
correctness_review.unchanged_semantics: Complete source diff and method AST comparison show activations is the only changed method. Initialization, state keys/load/export, external mixed-precision casts, optional embedding normalization, attention/masks/position IDs, rotary/query scaling, final norm, loss and optimizer paths are untouched.
correctness_review.jit: Embedding axis tuple is computed solely from static NativeLlamaSharding config. No array-dependent Python control flow, dynamic shape or device/backend query is introduced.

test_review.reference_independence: Expanded matrix compares the same native class with distinct no-FSDP/no-TP parameter placement against the selected sharded layout. This is a useful independent placement reference, not an independent model implementation. Existing named-model FP32/BF16 logits/loss/all-gradient parity provides the separate implementation anchor.
test_review.meaningful_behavior: Public full-model outputs, loss, every gradient leaf, checkpoint values and physical parameter/gradient/logit placement are checked. The expanded matrix also passes before the source edit; it verifies preservation/generalization, not the specific historical BF16 discrepancy.
test_review.tolerances: Existing 1e-5 atol/rtol retained; no numerical threshold or seed weakening.
nonblocking_gaps: Expanded multi-device layout matrix uses FP32, so it does not directly catch BF16 scatter accumulation/grouping divergence. Existing single-device named BF16 coverage cannot establish that multi-device property.

No extracted-candidate TPU all-gradient, 255-gradient acceptance, trajectory or full-Trainer gate has run in this review. These are future campaign/adoption evidence, not prerequisites to maintaining the narrow ordinary-JAX placement source change.
CPU explicit sharding validates legal forward/AD placement and numerics but does not establish TPU lowering, communication volume, memory, latency or throughput.

The TP-only case retains a size-one data mesh axis because of an existing loss fallback; renamed-axis cases with explicit batch sharding cover general embedding names. This is not evidence that the unrelated implicit loss fallback accepts an arbitrary axis-free mesh.

validation_evidence.affected_runner: Dry-run selection only; author ran selected native tests plus native benchmark/explicit-trainer tests manually with root markers and pinned existing environment. This is not evidence of executing the workspace installer.

scientific_evidence_boundary.interpretation: Supports this narrow layout hypothesis, not the original full-model failure cause or extracted-candidate full-Trainer acceptance. Synthetic inputs are not captured full-model weights/cotangents. Feature view is not more exact than legacy against the FP32 diagnostic.
